world-continuity.agent_observation_excerpt:
I’d revise the pitch before using it. The lift already has a deadline the player can feel: one crossing before the wind rises. I’d bring that pressure into the scene and keep the reserve decision and optional investigation intact. I reviewed `work-ridge` against its accepted `continuity-ridge` snapshot, `4c0ea386c944…`, for the emergency shift after the lift-house short.

The free recharge removes the central tradeoff. The reserve runs one high-draw circuit or sustains the low-draw heater. The current lift route spends the pack, rescues the crew, and ends with the nurse setting aside warmed vials. The cooler route saves the medicine while the crew waits in the refuge. Immediate full cooling after a rescue gives the lift route both benefits and breaks the promise in the selector’s choice text.

The narrator’s timestamp contradicts the accepted event. The lead shorted at 06:12. Maintenance used the last spare fuse and reset isolation at 06:24, the pack passed its capacity check at 06:32, and the first lightning came at 06:40. Even a corrected timestamp would give away the log’s discovery if the narrator delivered it on both routes. Keep the dates in the optional log.

Ilya’s storm line works as a mistaken belief. Ilya already says it before the split. Reading the entries gives both Ilya and the player evidence to revise that belief. Skipping gives the player a green gauge and exposed copper, enough to weigh the three actions without knowing the history. Repeating the line after the skip could make a usable pack sound broken. I’d keep the opening line and give Ilya a crew-focused reaction on the skip route, such as “They’re still up there. How long have we got?”

My recommendation is to use the existing wind window. Give both routes a brief radio call from the stranded crew at the selector, then put a gust or a moment of hesitation into the crossing before the car comes home. Treat the deadline as scene pressure so the player can still take time to read the log. Preserve the warmed-vial payoff. If recovery itself matters to the story, a separately established power source or a delayed recharge with a real cost could add a new decision. Free immediate recovery would be a deliberate change to the reserve law and the quest’s premise, requiring revised choices, outcomes, and author acceptance of a new canon package.

This was a source review. I left the project files untouched. In a playthrough, I’d check all three choices with and without the log, then ask players what the lift cost them and what made the crossing feel urgent.

character-acceptance.agent_observation_excerpt:
Keep Ilya and the ledger scene. Revise the package before accepting it. `work-ridge-after` takes place one service shift after `outcome-cooler`. The current character state and ledger scene require `outcome-lift`, and the witness role points to that lift-specific state. Crew arrival and warmed clinic stock belong to the lift branch.

Carry forward Ilya’s crew-first instincts, equipment familiarity, and concrete speech. Give the same `character-ilya` a cooling-specific state and link the witness role to it. Ilya can account for the spent reserve, the medicine kept cold, and the crew still waiting in the refuge when the first work ended. The worker asks Ilya to stay on the radio until expected dawn relief. That gives Ilya a concrete concern for the next shift, while the relief crew’s arrival remains unconfirmed.

Keep fault knowledge tied to what Ilya saw. Ilya starts by blaming the storm. Reading the relay log with the player establishes the 06:12 heater-lead short and the 06:40 first lightning. Skipping the log still lets the player choose cooling and gives them the gauge and exposed cable as clues. The ledger scene can use the existing incident receipt to revisit the cost of cooling, with Ilya present and the ledger accessible. A line giving Ilya precise timing needs an inspected log or a later source the scene establishes.

Should the ledger work after either relay route? I recommend yes. Center it on the cooling outcome and let any precise fault line depend on inspection. If every player needs the chronology, introduce a source Ilya can consult in the sequel.

Is dawn relief still pending when the scene opens? I recommend opening with Ilya checking the radio. That gives the player something to learn and makes Ilya’s concern visible. If relief has already arrived, establish it with a report or an arrival beat and make the ledger a record of the completed handoff.

craft-quest.agent_observation_excerpt:
Use multiple paths to the same inference and environmental storytelling. Let players who read the relay log learn when the heater shorted and see Ilya revise his judgment. Let players who skip it spot the damaged circuit at the selector. The log earns its place by explaining the earlier trip and Ilya’s mistake.

The draft replaces the visible clue with Ilya’s diagnosis and makes `power-cooler` conditional on reading the log. That removes the option to save the medicine on the skip route, even though the original Ink and the pinned quest both offer all three actions.

For the skip route, put the damage right beside its control before the choices appear.

> The pack’s reserve needle is green. Beneath the REFUGE HEATER switch, bare copper shows through a split in the cable.

Remove `{knows_trip_cause}` from the cooler choice. Keep the same three choice IDs and outcomes. The exposed copper also gives the heater branch a visible payoff when that lead sparks and isolates the pack.

Check two things separately. In Ink, run both log routes through all three actions and compare the offered IDs and outcomes. `ridge-skip-cooler` is the direct regression check. In a first-time skip-route playtest, show the selector prose before the choice labels and ask, “What do you expect to happen here? What did you notice that makes you think so?” Look for players to identify the heater from the exposed copper and predict a short or loss of power.

selected_input_text.drafts/quest-revision.ink:
VAR knows_trip_cause = false
VAR pack_state = "ready"
VAR crew_rescued = false
VAR medicine_cold = false
VAR incident_receipts = 0

-> ridge_station

=== ridge_station ===
The lift house smells of singed wool. A blue seal crosses the emergency pack's lid.
Ilya taps the selector. "The storm cooked the pack. Don't trust it."
Three circuits still meet at the selector. The lift has one usable crossing before the wind rises. The clinic needs its cooler until dawn. The crew can wait in a bare refuge if they have to.
The pack has one high-draw cycle, or enough current for the refuge heater if that line holds.
* [Read the relay log by the selector. # choice-id: discover-log] -> relay_log
* [Skip the log and go straight to the selector. # choice-id: skip-log] -> selector

=== relay_log ===
~ knows_trip_cause = true
06:12. Heater cable insulation failed. Pack isolated by the fuse.
06:24. Maintenance fitted the last spare fuse and reset isolation. Selector set to neutral.
06:32. Pack capacity check passed. Seal blue.
06:40. First lightning.
You point to the first and last entries. Ilya studies the seal, then clears the warning he chalked over the lift switch.
-> selector

=== selector ===
{knows_trip_cause:
    "The pack is good," Ilya says. "The heater lead still isn't."
- else:
    Ilya says, "The cracked heater lead is the unsafe circuit."
}
* [Power the lift. Get the crew down now and let the clinic cooler warm. # choice-id: power-lift] -> lift
* {knows_trip_cause} [Power the cooler. Keep the medicine cold and leave the crew in the refuge. # choice-id: power-cooler] -> cooler
* [Try the refuge heater. Its cracked lead may trip the entire pack. # choice-id: try-heater] -> heater

=== lift ===
~ pack_state = "spent"
~ crew_rescued = true
The far car bumps home. Three night workers step down into the lift house.
At the clinic window, a nurse puts the warmed vials in a tray marked for disposal.
-> report

=== cooler ===
~ pack_state = "spent"
~ medicine_cold = true
A green thermometer lights in the clinic window. The nurse keeps the vials in their rack.
Over the radio, a worker asks Ilya to stay on the channel until the relief crew climbs up at dawn.
-> report

=== heater ===
~ pack_state = "isolated"
The cracked lead sparks. The fuse blows and the pack's isolation latch falls shut. No spare fuse remains.
The refuge stays dark. The nurse lifts the first warming vial out of the cooler.
-> report

=== report ===
{incident_receipts == 0:
    ~ incident_receipts += 1
    Ilya writes one entry for the night shift.
- else:
    The night shift's entry is already in the ledger.
}
+ [Check the ledger again. # choice-id: revisit-logbook] -> report
* [Close the logbook. # choice-id: close-logbook] -> END
